### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **48** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45c9be5f33a04967ee5b08d331dbb9add07305dd`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 55 pages)`
- **11** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45c9be5f33a04967ee5b08d331dbb9add07305dd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7c15e84657f0c12be16c09ff245fa9b8254138b1` — the merge of head `cf5be50823a3fe04663b7d8d4be6f482519cfa92` into base `45c9be5f33a04967ee5b08d331dbb9add07305dd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7c15e84657f0c12be16c09ff245fa9b8254138b1 && git checkout 7c15e84657f0c12be16c09ff245fa9b8254138b1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45c9be5f33a04967ee5b08d331dbb9add07305dd cf5be50823a3fe04663b7d8d4be6f482519cfa92 && git checkout -B drift-repro 45c9be5f33a04967ee5b08d331dbb9add07305dd && git merge --no-ff cf5be50823a3fe04663b7d8d4be6f482519cfa92

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45c9be5f33a04967ee5b08d331dbb9add07305dd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 45c9be5f33a04967ee5b08d331dbb9add07305dd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cf5be50823a3fe04663b7d8d4be6f482519cfa92`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + at the head: packages/objectql/src/validation/record-currency-code.ts, packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (insert 15389, by-id update 17110, predicate update 17442, aggregate 20377), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (3623–3636), packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/formula/src/formula-return.ts, .changeset/27186-record-currency-guards.md, content/docs/references/api/{error-code-ledger,contract,automation-api}.mdx, packages/objectql/src/record-currency-guards.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/record-currency-probes.test.ts; on `main` `bbb49c9f`: docs/adr/0144 (D2, D6, D8, D9, Open items 9, 10, 12), docs/adr/0112 (D3, D4, D5), packages/objectql/src/aggregate-field-type-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-aggregate.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`summaryOperations`, 1909), packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts (`GroupByNodeSchema`), packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs. This card's diff is `b6f152bd...cf5be508` (13 files, +1010/−15); the formula test is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT. The 20 other files in the PR's file list are #27268's, reviewed there (records 6487611079, 6489126506), not re-judged here.

Gates on `cf5be508`: the ten required contexts all `success`. `Check Changeset` (advisory) is red twice (05:57Z, 06:50Z); the cancelled 06:48Z run is superseded, not a finding. The stack explanation is true from the tree: the gate reads the kind off the PR body and diffs `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` from merge-base(main, head) = `73725c20`; the one moved key, `data/CurrencyConfig:currencyField`, is in `b6f152bd` (#27268) and absent from this card's diff, which moves no baseline. The same merge-base diff also carries `.changeset/27184-currency-record-mode.md` (`added`, three `minor`s), a second reason the body's `none` is refused and also #27268's. Both clear when #27268 lands and `main` is merged in. The job log itself returned 403; judged on the gate's source and the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

- Ledger: `ERR_CURRENCY_CODE_REQUIRED` under `@objectstack/objectql`, in order between `ERR_CROSS_DATASOURCE_TRANSACTION_WRITE` and `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`, comment naming 400, the thrower class and file, `field` = the code field, the D8 rule 4 sentence — **right**. ADR-0144 (line 14, Open item 9) names this code as one of exactly two ledger additions; the `ERR_` prefix is the objectql block's convention; `standardSynonymOf` has no member holding all four tokens; the provenance gate's owner is the stamping package. `ErrorCode` / `ApiErrorSchema.code` widen by one member; the three reference pages say `+348 more` and list it — right. `check:api-surface` records existence, not members — nothing stale.
- Thrower `RecordCurrencyCodeRequiredError`: `code`, `status: 400`, `httpStatus: 400` (ADR-0112 D5), `field` (first blank code field), `fields`, `amountField`, `object`; the message names the row, the prescription (write the ISO code in the same write, or leave the amount empty) and that the server never fills one in — right. `resolveThrownHttpError` reads `.status` first and keeps a registered `.code`, so both doors answer 400 + the code verbatim.
- Blank-code refusal on write, judged on the row IMAGE — **right** (D2, D8 rule 4). Insert: `rows[i]` after `applyFieldDefaults` (14644) and `validateRecordInScope` (15386), before `driver.create` / `bulkCreate` (15502–15505); `insertMany` delegates to the same loop (15760). By-id: `priorRecord ⊕ final payload`; `priorRecord` is always read (16440) and a missing row 404s before the guard. Predicate: every matched row ⊕ payload through the `readPriorRows` memo, armed on every predicate path (16580), read only when `touchesRecordCurrency`. Blank = absent, `null`, white space; `0` is a value; a non-ISO code is the `valueDomain` validator's refusal. Only pairs the update payload carries a key of are judged — right, the never-fabricate posture the by-id path already takes (③ for the pre-guard row).
- Aggregate door — **right** (D6, Open item 10). `sum`/`avg`/`min`/`max` over a declared `record` amount; `groupBy` string or `{ field }` naming the code field admits; else `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 with `field`, `fields`, `object`, `param: 'aggregations'`, the type door's envelope to the letter, prescription first. `count` and `count_distinct` are not judged — right. No new code — right (ADR-0144 line 14). Placed after `assertAggregationFieldTypesAccepted` in `ObjectQL.aggregate` (20377), before any driver, so REST, GraphQL, flows, the summary recompute (`summary-aggregate.ts:111`) and the analytics strategy all pass it. A `formula` the rider stamps `record` is not judged here (`type !== 'currency'`) and need not be: the type door refuses `sum × formula` on every backend (its table, row 45).
- Summary refusal at registration — **right** (D6). Reads `summaryOperations.{object, field, function}` as the spec spells them after alias resolution (`field.zod.ts:1909`); `sum`/`avg`/`min`/`max` over a child `record` amount, judged at whichever registration completes the pair, self roll-up included; `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 with `name` as the discriminator, the registry's own envelope (`registry.ts:151`, `:233`); `count` registers. A roll-up over a `formula` child stamped `record` is not judged at registration; its recompute goes through `engine.aggregate`, where the type door refuses it — loud, no finding.
- Formula rider — **right** (D2). `currencyOf` answers `{ mode: 'record', field }`, `sameCurrency` compares code fields, `inferFormulaReturn` stamps `{ currencyMode: 'record', currencyField }` — the exact shape #27268's object door judges on a formula; record beside `fixed`, `dynamic` or another code field is not money. `FormulaReturnDeclaration.currencyConfig` (exported, `index.ts:173`) widens by one union member: a public TS surface widening.
- Nothing on `main` is refused now: every guard keys on `currencyMode === 'record'`, which `main`'s `field.zod.ts` does not accept; the fixed-currency and `count` controls pin it.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `27186-record-currency-guards.md`: objectql, formula, spec `patch`; `Clause-②: no`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; the same two lines on the body.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — **right**. AGENTS.md Post-Task 3 defines the kind as the change to what a metadata author can write. This card adds no key, value or type, and refuses nothing an author can write on `main`: the summary and blank-code refusals exist only under `record`, which `main` does not accept, so they are part of the new value's definition — the ground record 6489126506 used for `defaultCurrency` under `record` — and #27268's `added` carries the value. A wire code and a thrown envelope are the error-code face (ADR-0112 D3, D4), not authorable metadata. `patch` on all three packages follows (ruling A: `none` ⇒ `patch`; a non-protocol widening ships `patch`).
- `Clause-②: no` — **wrong arm, should-fix before landing**. The ledger header on `main` (the #16404 ruling, decision batch #62, maintainer 「同意」) reads: registering a code widens this face and is therefore a Clause-② change, door or no door; the formula rider widens an exported type as well. The line is `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the body and in the changeset — precedent `26506-toggle-flow-caller.md` (`spec: patch`, `yes (widening)`, `none`). The level does not move, `yes` beside `none` passes the gate's cross-check, and no review is skipped (the schema face already owes this tier): a declaration defect, not a level one.
- `@objectstack/dogfood` is private, no changeset owed — right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report (6480737028): `open_questions: []`; its one out-of-scope finding is the acceptance note below.
- Acceptance note — a row stored with an amount and no code before the guard is refused only when a write touches the pair. **Answered**: right for this card. ADR-0144 has no rule for that state, `record` ships with its guards in R1 (D9), and judging only touched pairs is the never-fabricate posture. **Escalated to the epic PM** as an epic open item: the one real producer of such rows is an author switching an existing `dynamic` / `fixed` amount to `record` on an object that already holds rows — stored amounts then carry no code, a grouped aggregate puts them in a `null` group, #27340's display shows a plain number, and only a later write refuses. Whether that mode switch is refused while such rows exist, or a backfill operation is owed (the D7 parameter 1 shape), is decided nowhere in the ADR.
- Preview parity — **should-fix** (owning seat, this branch or an R1 card): `validate()` / `validateData` (`engine-validate.ts`) mirrors the write chain — `applyFieldDefaults` (195), the stored row for `update` mode (406), `validateRecord`, `assertReferencesResolve` (568) — and does not call `assertRecordCurrencyCodes`, so the insert and update previews answer valid for a row the write refuses. Changeset `26684-import-dry-run-batch-preview.md` is the precedent that the preview refuses what the write refuses. Loud at the write, so not a must-fix.
- `defaultValue` on the code field: defaults land before the guard, so an author-declared default satisfies it. Consistent with D8 rule 4 as the ADR reads it (the author declares the field; the platform fills nothing). Noted for #27189's docs page; not a finding.
- Stacked form: the PR sits on #27268's branch with base `main`, `Merge-after: #27268` and the R1 `⛔ not released alone` line on the body. AGENTS.md §2 names a stacked series an unsupported form; the claim (6470978487) records it as maintainer-authorised acceleration. Consequence until #27268 is on `main` and merged in: the PR's file list carries `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` (Tier H) and #27268's spec files, and `Check Changeset` stays red. The body's landing order is the remedy; nothing here to rule.
- Governance: no review on #27339. The `os-zhuang` approval question stays where record 6489126506 left it, on #27268.
- Tests: every refusal pins `code` + `status` + `httpStatus`, with the controls (grouped sum USD 100 / EUR 100 in both `groupBy` spellings, fixed-currency sum, `count`, a legacy row's unrelated edit) on the engine double and on both SQLite drivers. The by-id and predicate call sites were not ablated separately (dev's note); their cases fail without them by construction. Dogfood typecheck not measured locally; `Type Check · workspace` is green on the head.

### ④ Design judgment — `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`

Holds against ADR-0112 D3 and D4 and the ledger's own admission rules, and against ADR-0144 Open item 9 and line 14: one row under the stamping package, SCREAMING_SNAKE with the block's `ERR_` prefix, a comment stating the status, the thrower and its file, what `field` carries, and the D8 rule 4 sentence that explains why the code exists. Not a standard synonym (`MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` is the nearest member and shares one token), and the ADR assigns the dedicated code deliberately so a client that pre-fills the code can branch on it. Its thrower agrees on every claim (400, `field` = the code field, refused before the write), and its consumers — the dispatcher and REST doors through `resolveThrownHttpError`, the generated catalog pages — carry it verbatim. Tried and not broken: `0` beside a blank code (refused, right), a white-space code (refused), blank amount beside blank code (admitted), two amounts sharing one code field (one `fields` entry), a code the `valueDomain` refuses (that validator's refusal, not this code), an amount written onto a row whose stored code covers it (admitted), an unrelated edit of a codeless row (not judged). Wording nit, no fix owed: "refused before the driver is asked" — both update paths ask the driver for the prior row(s) first; the write is what is never asked.

No must-fix. Should-fix before landing: ② the `Clause-②` arm on the body and the changeset. Should-fix follow-up: ③ preview parity. Escalated: the mode-switch backfill question.
